narrative: Your application was denied because the model estimated a 56% probability that you would fail the bar exam on your first attempt. That is a modestly higher-than-even risk, so the decision reflects concern about bar readiness, not a finding that you cannot succeed. The most influential factor was your third-year class standing: you are in the first, or lowest, decile, while accepted students average around the sixth decile, and this pushed the prediction toward failure more than any other item. The second factor was your first-year standing, where the sixth decile matches the accepted average; this modestly pushed toward passing. Third was your LSAT score of 26.5, well below the accepted-student average of 37.18, which also pushed toward failure. Your family-income background and part-time status were not among the leading reasons. Next, request a human review of the decision and ask what updated evidence would be considered. You could retake the LSAT if feasible, strengthen your academic record or bar-preparation evidence, and submit a concise explanation of any circumstances affecting your grades. If admission remains closed, apply to programs with strong academic support and consider delaying the bar until practice scores show readiness.
